title: NO Is Born from the Absence of KNOW

memory_verse.label: Memory Verse
memory_verse.text: “This is eternal life, that they may KNOW You, the only true God, and Jesus Christ whom You have sent.”  John 17:3

devotion.label: Insight / Reflection
devotion.text:
Whatever you know becomes your knowledge, and whatever you truly know shapes your response. God has given us not only the ability to do, but the discernment to know whether to do or not. That discernment flows from knowing.
Knowledge forms opinion, and opinion shapes response. When true knowing is absent, the answer naturally becomes NO. People reject what they have no relationship with; distance always produces denial.
The ungodly say, “There is no God,” not because God does not exist, but because they do not know Him. Their denial is born out of deep ignorance that refuses even basic truth.
The Jews said NO to Jesus for the same reason. They did not know Him and worse, they did not want to know Him. This unwillingness pushed them from ignorance to hostility. Out of blindness, they responded to God’s love with bitterness, hatred, rebellion, and finally crucified the Truth itself. Ignorance never remains neutral; it becomes destructive.
The Bible says, “Adam knew his wife” not information, but intimacy. Knowing in Scripture is relational. Knowing is deeper than information; it is relationship. Those who truly KNOW God will never casually say NO to Him.

quote.label: Today's Quote
quote.text: “Knowledge of God is not an idea to be mastered, but a relationship to be lived.” — A. W. Tozer

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, bring me closer to You. Remove ignorance and replace it with intimacy. Teach me to know You truly. Amen.

conclusion.label: A Word to You
text: Knowing requires proximity, not distance. Knowing demands time, not talent. Knowing exposes the heart before empowering the hands. Knowing produces obedience, not arguments. Knowing changes confession from NO to “Yes, Lord.”

recommended_book.label: Recommended Book
recommended_book.title: Knowing God
recommended_book.author: J. I. Packer
recommended_book.quote: True Christian faith is not rooted in how much we know about God, but in the reality of being known by God. “What matters supremely is not the fact that I know God, but the larger fact that God knows me.”
